per_cycle_phases: RESET: [RST_I] asserted; MASTER drives [STB_O]=0, [CYC_O]=0 (RULE 3.20); SLAVE's self-starting state machines initialize at the rising [CLK_I] after [RST_I] (RULE 3.15).
CYCLE_INITIATE: MASTER asserts [CYC_O] (and optionally [TGC_O], [LOCK_O]) to indicate a valid bus cycle is starting.
PHASE_REQUEST: MASTER asserts [STB_O] together with the address/data/control qualifying signals ([ADR_O], [DAT_O] on write, [SEL_O], [WE_O], [TAGN_O]).
WAIT (optional): MASTER and/or SLAVE inserts wait states — MASTER by keeping [STB_O] LOW between phases (-WSM-), SLAVE by keeping [ACK_O]/[ERR_O]/[RTY_O] LOW after [STB_I] asserted (-WSS-).
PHASE_ACK: SLAVE asserts one of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], [RTY_O] (RULE 3.45 — at most one).
PHASE_TERMINATE: At the next rising [CLK_I], MASTER negates [STB_O]; SLAVE then negates its termination signal.
CYCLE_TERMINATE: After the last phase's [STB_O] negation, MASTER negates [CYC_O] (and [TGC_O], [LOCK_O]).
fsm_hints_standard_handshake.single_cycle_rule: RULE 3.25 — [CYC_O] asserted no later than [STB_O] assertion; negated no earlier than [STB_O] negation.
fsm_hints_standard_handshake.block_cycle_rule: BLOCK cycles wrap multiple [STB_O]+[ACK_I] phases inside a single [CYC_O] assertion. [LOCK_O] is typically asserted by the MASTER during a BLOCK cycle to retain ownership of a shared SLAVE across an arbitration boundary.
fsm_hints_standard_handshake.rmw_cycle_rule: RMW cycles wrap one READ phase + one WRITE phase inside a single [CYC_O] assertion. [WE_O] is flipped between the two phases. The cycle is atomic from the bus arbitration standpoint.
master_per_phase_fsm: PHASE_DRIVE: drive [ADR_O], [DAT_O] (on write), [SEL_O], [WE_O], [TAGN_O] valid; assert [CYC_O] and [STB_O] (and [TGC_O], [LOCK_O] as needed). Hold these signals stable until the SLAVE acknowledges.
SLAVE_WAIT: if [ACK_I]=[ERR_I]=[RTY_I]=0, stay in PHASE_DRIVE (SLAVE inserting wait states -WSS-).
PHASE_TERMINATE: on rising [CLK_I] with a termination signal asserted, latch read data on [DAT_I] (if read), negate [STB_O]; if this was the last phase, also negate [CYC_O] (and [TGC_O], [LOCK_O]).
MASTER_WAIT: between phases of a multi-phase cycle (BLOCK or RMW), MASTER MAY keep [STB_O] LOW for any number of cycles while still holding [CYC_O]=1 — this is a master-driven wait state -WSM-.
slave_per_phase_fsm: SAMPLE: on every rising [CLK_I], check [CYC_I] AND [STB_I]; if both HIGH, this phase is targeting this SLAVE (after partial-decode of [ADR_I]).
DRIVE_RESPONSE: drive valid [DAT_O()] (for read) and assert exactly ONE of [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] (RULE 3.45) in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] AND [STB_I] (RULE 3.35).
DRIVE_WAIT_STATE: if SLAVE is not yet ready, keep [ACK_O]=[ERR_O]=[RTY_O]=0 — this inserts -WSS- wait state(s); MASTER will hold [STB_O] until SLAVE responds.
PHASE_END: when MASTER negates [STB_O], SLAVE negates its termination signal (RULE 3.50).

fsm_hints_pipelined_handshake.principle: In pipelined mode the MASTER does not wait for [ACK_I] before outputting the next request. The [STALL_I] input throttles the MASTER pipeline.
master_pipelined_fsm: REQ: drive request on [ADR_O]/[DAT_O]/[SEL_O]/[WE_O], assert [CYC_O] and [STB_O].
REQ_STALL: while [STALL_I]=1, hold all request signals; [STB_O] remains asserted.
REQ_ADVANCE: when [STALL_I]=0, the slave has accepted the request — on the next rising [CLK_I] the MASTER MAY drive a new request (or negate [STB_O] if no more requests).
PIPE_DRAIN: after all requests issued, wait for the remaining outstanding [ACK_I] pulses; after the LAST [ACK_I], negate [CYC_O] to end the cycle.
slave_pipelined_fsm: SAMPLE: on every rising [CLK_I], if [CYC_I] AND [STB_I] AND NOT [STALL_O] AND (WE_I matches), capture the request into the queue.
STALL: if internal pipeline cannot accept another request, drive [STALL_O]=1 — the MASTER will hold its current request next cycle.
ACK_DRIVE: independently of [STB_I], drive [ACK_O]=1 for each completed transaction; for reads, drive valid [DAT_O()] on the cycle [ACK_O]=1.

fsm_hints_registered_feedback_burst.principle: Chapter 4 — uses [CTI_O()] and [BTE_O()] Address Tags to advertise the cycle type to the SLAVE so the SLAVE can prepare its response in advance (avoiding the inherent wait state of a synchronous-termination scheme).
burst_state_transitions: START_BURST: MASTER asserts [CYC_O]+[STB_O] with [CTI_O()]={'001' (constant address burst) | '010' (incrementing burst)}; [BTE_O()] indicates wrap size for incrementing bursts; SLAVE recognizes the burst type and prepares response.
MID_BURST_BEAT: every cycle (or with SLAVE wait states), MASTER drives next address (or holds constant for constant-address) and SLAVE asserts [ACK_I]; [CTI_O()] stays at the burst type.

LAST_BEAT: on the last beat, MASTER changes [CTI_O()]=3'b111 (End-of-Burst) at the same clock edge as the last [STB_O]; SLAVE recognizes End-of-Burst and prepares to terminate the burst rather than expect another beat.
BURST_TERMINATE: after the last [ACK_I], MASTER negates [STB_O] and [CYC_O]; cycle ends.

anti_deadlock_rule.watchdog_recommendation: RECOMMENDATION 3.10 — Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution is to include a watchdog timer that monitors the MASTER's [STB_O] signal and asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit.
anti_deadlock_rule.registered_outputs_rule: RECOMMENDATION 3.15 — Design WISHBONE MASTER interfaces so that there are no intermediate logic gates between a registered flip-flop and the signal outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O]. Delay timing for [STB_O] and [CYC_O] are very often the most critical paths in the system.
anti_deadlock_rule.no_combinational_loop_rule: OBSERVATION 3.50 — In large high-speed designs the asynchronous assertion of [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] could lead to unacceptable delay times caused by the loopback delay from the MASTER to the SLAVE and back to the MASTER. Using registered [ACK_O]/[ERR_O]/[RTY_O] significantly reduces this loopback delay (at the cost of one additional wait state per transfer).

exit_from_reset.wishbone: Earliest the MASTER may assert [STB_O] / [CYC_O] is the rising [CLK_I] edge following the negation of [RST_I] (OBSERVATION 3.05). All self-starting state machines force themselves to a defined initial state (RULE 3.15).

default_ready_state_recommendation.wishbone: When the SLAVE guarantees it can keep pace with all MASTER interfaces and the [ERR_I] / [RTY_I] signals are not used, the SLAVE's [ACK_O] signal MAY be tied to the logical AND of the SLAVE's [STB_I] and [CYC_I] inputs (PERMISSION 3.10). PERMISSION 3.35 — Under certain circumstances SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to hold [ACK_O] in the asserted state (point-to-point single-SLAVE no-wait-state case).

transfer_signal_constancy_during_phase_c: MASTER MUST hold [ADR_O], [DAT_O] (on write), [SEL_O], [WE_O], [TAGN_O], [TGA_O], [TGC_O] stable from when it asserts [STB_O] until the SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] / [ERR_I] / [RTY_I] (i.e. these signals are qualified by [STB_O] per RULE 3.60).
Between phases of a BLOCK or RMW cycle, the MASTER MAY change these signals before re-asserting [STB_O] for the next phase.

evidence.quote: All WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I]. The following MASTER signals MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]: [STB_O], [CYC_O]. The state of all other MASTER signals are undefined in response to a reset cycle.

The MASTER asserts [STB_O] when it is ready to transfer data. [STB_O] remains asserted until the SLAVE asserts one of the cycle terminating signals [ACK_I], [ERR_I] or [RTY_I]. At every rising edge of [CLK_I] the terminating signal is sampled. If it is asserted, then [STB_O] is negated.

If a SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, then the SLAVE MUST NOT assert more than one of [ACK_O], [ERR_O] or [RTY_O]. SLAVE interfaces MUST be designed so that the [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] signals are asserted and negated in response to the assertion and negation of [STB_I].

Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution to this problem is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER's [STB_O] signal, and asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit.
Design WISHBONE MASTER interfaces so that there are no intermediate logic gates between a registered flip-flop and the signal outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O].

In pipelined mode the master doesn't wait for [ACK_I] before outputting next address/data word on the bus. We have a [STALL_I] input in the master, indicating that the slave pipeline can accept another request at the moment. Master outputs the requests as long as [STALL_I] is low. When [STALL_I] is asserted, it waits.

WISHBONE Registered Feedback bus cycles use the Cycle Type Identifier [CTI_O()], [CTI_I()] Address Tags to implement the advanced synchronous cycle termination scheme. Both MASTER and SLAVE interfaces must support [CTI_O()], [CTI_I()] in order to provide the improved bandwidth. Additional information about the type of burst is provided by the Burst Type Extension [BTE_O()], [BTE_I()] Address Tags.
